AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To describe the incidence of overuse musculoskeletal injuries in service members with combat-related lower limb amputation.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: A total of 791 service members with deployment-related lower limb injury: 496 with a major lower limb amputation and 295 with a mild lower limb injury.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
AbstractText.content: The outcomes of interest were clinical diagnosis codes (International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision [ICD-9]) associated with musculoskeletal overuse injuries of the lumbar spine, upper limb, and lower limb regions one year before and one year after injury.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The overall incidence of developing at least one musculoskeletal overuse injury within the first year after lower limb amputation was between 59-68%. Service members with unilateral lower limb amputation were almost twice as likely to develop an overuse lower or upper limb injury as compared to those with mild combat-related injury. Additionally, service members with bilateral lower limb amputation were more than twice as likely to develop a lumbar spine injury and four times more likely to develop an upper limb overuse injury within the first year after amputation as compared to those with mild combat-related injury.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Incidence of secondary overuse musculoskeletal injury is elevated in service members with lower limb amputation and warrants focused research efforts towards developing preventive interventions.
